judged_text: LarkCalendarService.createEvent uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) without matching on the credentialId passed under the new Calendar interface, unlike the Google implementation this diff adds. For collective events whose first destination calendar belongs to a different credential/provider, Lark creates the event on the wrong calendar or throws 'no calendar id', so collective members on Lark get no (or a misdirected) calendar event while the booking proceeds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` and updates GoogleCalendarService to select the destination calendar by matching `credentialId` against `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`. However, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` still has the old signature `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and now derives `calendarId` from only the first element of the (now-array) `event.destinationCalendar` via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`. Meanwhile, EventManager now builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (including additional team members for COLLECTIVE) and `createAllCalendarEvents` iterates destinations/credentials but passes the same `event` object each time. For Lark credentials, this means it will always use destinationCalendar[0] rather than the calendar matching the credential being processed, causing events to be created on the wrong calendar (or to throw `no calendar id` if the first destination is not a valid Lark calendar). This is a correctness defect grounded in the diff.
